text_blocks.snippet: A FODMAP diet, more accurately a low-FODMAP diet, is a dietary approach that restricts certain types of carbohydrates to manage digestive symptoms, particularly for individuals with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). FODMAP stands for Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols, which are types of carbohydrates that can be poorly absorbed in the small intestine and may cause digestive distress in some individuals.
snippet_highlighted_words: a dietary approach that restricts certain types of carbohydrates to manage digestive symptoms, particularly for individuals with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of the FODMAP diet:

list.title: Purpose:
list.snippet: The diet is primarily used to identify and manage foods that trigger digestive symptoms like gas, bloating, abdominal pain, and diarrhea, often associated with IBS.

list.title: How it works:
list.snippet: By temporarily eliminating high-FODMAP foods, individuals can reduce the fermentation process in the gut, which can alleviate digestive discomfort.
